title: Vector Databases — Trade a Little Recall for Speed
key_insight: Approximate nearest-neighbor methods organize likely neighborhoods. Search controls such as probe count trade more work for a better chance of finding the true top results.
body:
## Trade a Little Recall for Speed

An exact scan finds the true nearest items but checks everything. An approximate index skips much of the collection and may miss a rare neighbor.

Approximate nearest-neighbor methods organize likely neighborhoods. Search controls such as probe count trade more work for a better chance of finding the true top results.

Measure recall against an exact sample, along with latency. A fast index that misses the needed document is not useful.
common_mistakes: A vector database removes the need to store source text.
Approximate search is guaranteed to return the exact same neighbors.
Access control should be applied only after private text reaches the model.
mini_exercise: Draw “Trade a Little Recall for Speed” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Large retrieval systems need fast similarity search plus filters, updates, metadata, and operational guarantees.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Trade a Little Recall for Speed,” explain Vector Databases without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
